subject.title: Slug alias quota (25) blocking legitimate naming migration — publisher nitishgargiitd

question: Should a verified ClawHub operator authorize a one-time audited exception for publisher `nitishgargiitd` to preserve redirects for the 13 enumerated renames, or require selected old redirects to be released first?
rationale: The existing quota protects against long-term slug reservation and squatting; choosing an account-specific exception or redirect-release criteria is an authorization policy decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Authorize a scoped migration exception
options.body: Verify publisher ownership and allow only the 13 listed old-to-new redirect mappings with an audit record, while leaving the global cap unchanged.

options.title: Release selected old redirects first
options.body: Keep the cap strict and ask the publisher to identify older aliases that can be retired under documented traffic or install-compatibility criteria.

options.title: Define a reusable migration policy
options.body: Pause the account action until maintainers establish a documented exception workflow for legitimate large publisher renames.

recommendation.title: Authorize a scoped migration exception
recommendation.body: Verify publisher ownership and allow only the 13 listed old-to-new redirect mappings with an audit record, while leaving the global cap unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged anti-squatting work is the closest available history signal for preserving the intended security boundary during an exception decision.
